SEA-AD multiregional progression, tissue response and longitudinal cognitive phenotypes

Released Global/Local CPS against conventional staging, MG4 and NeuN in regional tissue, and four-domain cognitive level and decline in ACT

1. Scientific questions and cohort

This notebook links global AD progression, regional pathological involvement and cellular tissue response to longitudinal cognitive phenotypes. Morphology is still being processed.

Its first pass established four results from direct multiregional QNP:

  • MG4 is mainly donor-level and follows donor-wide tau.
  • Regional NeuN is weakly lower where regional tau is higher.
  • Executive decline behaves differently from memory decline.
  • Multiregional tau accounts for part of the cognitive “discordance” left by the MTG-fitted CPS.

Those results are kept (Sections 3 and 6). This amended version moves the progression representation onto the released multiregion progression scores, and it characterizes all four cognitive domains.

  1. Disease heterogeneity. How heterogeneous is quantitative progression within Braak and ADNC categories? How does local involvement vary among donors at comparable global progression? Which anatomical patterns appear across the available regions?
  2. Longitudinal cognitive phenotypes. How do terminal CASI, the global slope, and the level and rate of memory, executive, language and visuospatial function relate to global versus anatomically matched local pTau progression?
  3. Tissue response. Does MG4 follow global or region-specific pTau progression? Does regional NeuN vary with local pTau progression? Does MG4 carry tissue-integrity information at comparable local pathology?

Everything is cross-sectional postmortem tissue plus antemortem cognition. No association below is causal, establishes temporal order or mediation, or measures circuit function.

Progression source and definitions. Global_and_Local_CPS.20260105.csv from the multiregion release is used as released. Its columns are CPS_Global, CPS_Global_pTau, CPS_Global_ABeta, CPS_Local, CPS_Local_pTau and CPS_Local_ABeta.

  • Not re-derived. Nothing is re-estimated, averaged across regions, or combined into a new score.
  • Global and local are not independent exposures. They are never entered as if they were, and local is not treated as a residual from global.
  • Distinct from notebook 04’s CPS. CPS_Global is not SpecimenMetadata.csv’s Continuous Pseudo-progression Score (the Gabitto MTG CPS; notebook 01). The Gabitto-CPS analyses from this notebook’s first pass are kept for reference in Section 6 and are not repeated.

2. Disease heterogeneity: conventional staging and released progression

Staging as the reference. Braak stage and ADNC serve as the conventional frame; neither is read as disease time. Every quantity in this section is descriptive:

  • the spread of CPS_Global_pTau inside each stage;
  • the spread of CPS_Local_pTau in each region among donors in the same CPS_Global_pTau tertile;
  • each region’s median local pTau as global progression rises, which gives its anatomical ordering.

Reading.

  • Within staging, progression is heterogeneous. Global pTau CPS rises with Braak stage (ρ 0.87) and ADNC (ρ 0.84), but the categories overlap widely. Of the 34 Braak V donors, 6 sit below the highest Braak IV value and 26 above the lowest Braak VI value. Among the 42 High-ADNC donors, 13 sit below the highest Intermediate value. Braak V and High ADNC each span most of the global pTau range.
  • At comparable global progression, local involvement still varies. Local and global pTau correlate at ρ 0.79–0.92 across regions. In the middle global tertile, the local pTau IQR is 0.09–0.26 on a 0–1 scale. It is widest in the neocortical association regions reached at mid-stage (STG, FI, AnG), where donors of the same global stage differ most in how far tau has spread.
  • Anatomical pattern. At low global progression, local pTau is already highest in MEC and HIP (medians 0.59 and 0.46), while V1C is essentially uninvolved until the high tertile. That is the expected medial-temporal → association-cortex → primary-cortex sequence. The two neocortical core regions differ in shape: DFC already carries low-level pTau at low global stage (median 0.22 vs MTG 0.07) but rises mainly in the high tertile, whereas MTG rises steadily through mid-stage.
  • What the released local scores are. Local pTau CPS correlates with direct AT8 at ρ ≥ 0.97 in every region, and local Aβ CPS with direct 6E10 at ρ ≥ 0.99. In rank terms they are the direct stain measurements placed on a common progression scale, not independent observations. For the same reason, direct QNP and CPS are never entered as separate exposures of one pathology in the same model.
  • Global pTau vs global CPS vs Gabitto CPS. CPS_Global correlates with the Gabitto MTG CPS at ρ 0.84, and global pTau with global Aβ at ρ 0.70. The three are related but distinct released quantities.

3. Tissue response: MG4, NeuN and regional pathology

3.1 Direct QNP decomposition (first pass, retained)

Every regional measure is split into a donor-wide mean over MTG, DFC and MEC and a regional deviation from it. The fit is Mundlak within/between; the within-donor coefficient equals the donor fixed-effects estimate.

  • QNP measures: within-ROI normal scores.
  • MG4 and astrocyte activation: in pooled within-ROI SD units.
  • Intervals: 2000-resample donor-cluster bootstrap. (nlme and lme4 are not installed.)

First-pass reading, unchanged.

  • Donor-level states. After region differences are removed, a donor’s shared level carries 55% of MG4 variance and 61% of astrocyte-activation variance.
  • MG4 and tau. MG4 follows donor-wide AT8 (+0.37 [+0.09, +0.66] SD per SD) more than regional AT8 deviation (+0.14 [-0.03, +0.30]).
  • Amyloid adds nothing (+0.07 [-0.19, +0.32]).
  • GFAP is the measure dominated by within-donor regional variation.

3.2 MG4 against released global and local pTau progression

Three quantities on the same donor × ROI rows, each a separate model rather than one joint model of global and local:

  • (a) Global: MG4 ~ ROI + CPS_Global_pTau.
  • (b) Local, pooled: MG4 ~ ROI + CPS_Local_pTau.
  • (c) Local, within donor: MG4 ~ ROI + CPS_Local_pTau + donor, with donor fixed effects. Global progression is constant within a donor, so (c) asks whether a donor’s more-involved regions carry more MG4, with no averaging of CPS across regions and no residualization.
  1. and (b) are also compared by R², on identical rows. Exposures are per SD over the model rows.

Reading. MG4 follows global pTau progression:

  • Global: +0.36 [+0.20, +0.51] SD per SD in the core ROIs; +0.37 [+0.19, +0.54] across all regions.
  • Local, pooled: fits MG4 no better (R² difference -0.01 [-0.05, +0.02]; all regions -0.03 [-0.07, -0.00]).
  • Local, within donor: a donor’s more-involved regions do not carry clearly more MG4 (+0.16 [-0.08, +0.37]; all regions -0.00 [-0.13, +0.14]).

This reproduces the direct-QNP result of 3.1 on the released progression scale. MG4 is predominantly a donor-level response that scales with global pTau stage, and only weakly, if at all, a regional one.

3.3 Regional NeuN, local pTau progression and MG4

NeuN is a direct QNP measurement (within-ROI normal score of NeuN-positive cells per area). It is related to local pTau through the pTau-specific released score and through direct AT8, in separate models, never jointly.

CPS_Local_pTau is released as pTau-specific. Its construction is not documented locally, but it tracks direct AT8 at ρ ≥ 0.97 in every region (Section 2). Its correlation with NeuN matches that of direct AT8, which gives no sign that NeuN is among its inputs. The combined CPS_Local and the Gabitto CPS are not used with NeuN, since they may contain it.

Models, donor fixed effects throughout:

  • Within-donor coupling: NeuN ~ ROI + local pTau + donor.
  • MG4 at comparable local pathology: NeuN ~ ROI + local pTau + MG4 + donor.
  • First-pass direct-AT8 model, for comparison: the Mundlak model with donor-wide and regional AT8 and MG4, on balanced donors.

Reading.

  • NeuN and local pTau progression. Within donors, NeuN is lower where local pTau progression is higher (-0.13 [-0.33, +0.08] SD per SD), and the interval reaches zero. Direct AT8 gives the same result (-0.13 [-0.27, +0.01]). It is a modest, imprecise coupling, the same on both pathology representations.
  • MG4 at comparable local pathology. It adds at most weak information:
    • at comparable local pTau CPS: +0.09 [-0.06, +0.23];
    • at comparable direct AT8: +0.09 [-0.06, +0.23];
    • the first-pass regional-deviation estimate: +0.15 [+0.01, +0.26].
    The direction is consistent (relatively MG4-high regions have slightly higher NeuN), but only the first-pass Mundlak interval clears zero. It does so barely, and not once the two NeuN-floor donors are removed (+0.15 [-0.01, +0.28]). It is not evidence that MG4 preserves neurons.

3.4 Supporting check: the two donors with near-zero NeuN immunoreactivity

The two donors with near-zero NeuN immunoreactivity in all core ROIs. snRNA-seq share = neuronal nuclei / all nuclei recovered and retained in the release across the donor’s libraries in that region, from a separate tissue block. It reflects nuclei recovery, QC retention and SEA-AD’s nuclei enrichment design as well as tissue composition, and is not a neuron count.

H20.33.028 Y Braak V · High ADNC 75 DFC 29.4 (297) 0.68× 0.50 (0%) 0.27
H21.33.020 Y Braak V · High ADNC 77 DFC 6.7 (297) 0.55× 0.57 (3%) 0.70
H20.33.028 Y Braak V · High ADNC 75 MEC 7.5 (260) 0.43× 0.28 (4%) 0.82
H21.33.020 Y Braak V · High ADNC 77 MEC 3.7 (260) 1.22× 0.11 (0%) 0.84
H20.33.028 Y Braak V · High ADNC 75 MTG 7.9 (322) 0.58× 0.54 (4%) 0.56
H21.33.020 Y Braak V · High ADNC 77 MTG 0.3 (322) 0.60× 0.16 (0%) 0.64

Reading. Three things are kept apart here:

  • neuronal loss, meaning fewer neurons;
  • reduced NeuN immunoreactivity or an altered neuronal phenotype, meaning neurons present but poorly labelled;
  • differential recovery or representation of neuronal nuclei in snRNA-seq.

What the release documents. Both donors carry the published Severely Affected Donor flag (11 donors in all). 8 of the 10 sub-10%-of-median NeuN rows belong to severely affected donors. The dataset description (Gabitto et al., Research Square preprint rs-2921860) says these donors were identified by extreme snRNA-seq/snATAC-seq QC:

  • fewer UMIs and genes per nucleus;
  • a lower fraction of nuclei passing QC;
  • reduced nuclear-localized RNA.

The authors read this as transcriptional shutdown. They also report that these donors “had a pronounced reduction in neuron labeling (not due entirely to cell loss) for NeuN” and steeper late-life memory decline.

What this notebook observes.

  • NeuN immunoreactivity is near zero in every core ROI (down to 0.3 cells/mm²), and the detected NeuN-positive profiles are about half to two-thirds of the usual size in MTG and DFC.
  • snRNA-seq neuronal share is the lowest in every core ROI (≤ the 4th percentile).

What that supports. A severe neuronal phenotype with markedly reduced NeuN immunoreactivity. Absolute neuronal loss is neither established nor excluded:

  • reduced NeuN antigenicity can mimic loss in IHC;
  • because these donors were defined partly by poor nuclei QC, their low snRNA-seq neuronal share may reflect differential recovery or QC retention of neuronal nuclei rather than neuron number.

The two observations are consistent with each other, but they are not independent confirmation of depletion.

  • The MG4–NeuN reading does not depend on them. Removing these two donors changes the MG4 terms by less than 0.05 SD. Removing all severely affected donors moves them within their intervals (table in 3.3). They stay in every primary analysis, and the severely-affected flag is not used as an explanatory variable anywhere.

4. Longitudinal cognitive phenotypes (ACT, 69 donors)

4.1 Released variables: documentation, observations and open questions

The harmonized workbook is a single sheet with no notes, codebook or methods text. The SEA-AD data dictionary covers only Last CASI Score and its interval.

One focused search of the accessible methods literature found two usable sources:

  • The harmonization pipeline. It is described in Mukherjee et al. (2023, Neuropsychology 37: 409, doi 10.1037/neu0000835; full text not accessible here) and, in methods text, in the cohort-pooled genome-wide study of these scores (Mol Neurodegener 2023, PMC10286470).
  • The dataset paper. The Gabitto et al. preprint cites Crane et al. (2022, Alzheimer’s & Dementia 18:e064534) for the domain scores. Crane and Mukherjee are listed data contributors of the SEA-AD metadata release. The preprint’s full Methods were not accessible.

Why do 58% of visuospatial visits share one value? The score distribution suggests an answer, though no document states it:

VSP_E in ACT: share of visits at and above the modal value (0.609) by time before death.
Years before death Visits At modal value Above modal value
0–3 52 50% 8%
4–7 134 63% 4%
8–12 156 31% 26%
> 12 197 78% 1%
  • Few distinct values. ACT VSP_E takes 52 distinct values over 539 visits, against 262 for MEM_E.
  • An identical scored pattern. The modal value 0.609 holds 58% of visits and 67 of 69 donors reach it at least once. Every modal visit carries the same SE (0.859), which is what an identical item set with an identical response pattern produces.
  • Not the scale maximum. Only 10% of visits score above it (up to 1.20), and those carry lower SEs (median 0.76), as expected when more items were administered.
  • Empirical reading. The pattern is consistent with a ceiling on a small, routinely administered visuospatial item set, with higher scores reachable only at visits with additional items. The share at the mode also varies non-monotonically with time before death, which suggests battery composition changed across ACT waves.
  • Status. Neither the item content nor the battery history is documented in the accessible sources. This remains an empirical explanation, not a documented one. VSP_E and slope_zvsp0 are kept as released, not rescaled or replaced.

Released slopes against the visits. Each released slope is compared with the ordinary least-squares rate of the same donor’s visits. That rate is a check only; it is never used as an outcome.

Released domain slopes against each donor’s own OLS rate (score per year of age). No standard error is released for any slope.
Domain Variable Donors r with OLS rate Slope on OLS rate Mean offset SD ratio
Memory slope_zmem0 69 0.88 0.99 -0.05 1.13
Executive slope_zexf0 69 0.73 0.46 -0.02 0.64
Language slope_zlan0 69 0.73 0.64 -0.03 0.88
Visuospatial slope_zvsp0 69 0.34 0.28 -0.04 0.81
  • slope_zmem0 (memory decline). Behaves like a per-year MEM_E rate (coefficient 0.99 on the donors’ OLS rates, r 0.88), with a mean offset.
  • slope_zexf0 and slope_zlan0 (executive and language decline). Shrunk toward the mean (SD ratios 0.64 and 0.88), consistent with model-based person-specific estimates.
  • slope_zvsp0 (visuospatial decline). Agrees poorly with the visits (r 0.34).
  • slope_zcasi_irt0 (global decline). An IRT-scaled CASI slope that cannot be checked against visits, since no visit-level score is released. It is the only global longitudinal rate.

The exact models, units and uncertainty of all five slopes remain unresolved. They are used as released, never replaced by the OLS rates, and never given assumed standard errors. Coefficients on slopes are therefore reported in SD of the released variable, not in cognitive units per year.

Reading.

  • Memory and language both decline measurably, and in both the rate correlates with terminal CASI (ρ 0.74 and 0.60).
  • Executive function declines more slowly. Its rate is related to terminal CASI more weakly (0.39).
  • Visuospatial scores sit largely on one value (58% of visits). The domain has a coarse ceiling, and its rate is essentially unrelated to terminal CASI (0.09). Memory and language also show ceiling clusters (25% and 38% of visits at one value), so early decline from high performers is poorly resolved.
  • Level and rate are moderately correlated within each domain, but they are not interchangeable.
  • A single visit is noisy. Visit-level standard errors are comparable to the between-visit SD for memory and language, and larger than it for executive and visuospatial scores.

Grouped-trajectory diagnostic (Figure 2C). The binned trajectories pool whichever donors were seen at each time before death. Two checks follow: how many donors feed each bin, and whether the within-donor change over each donor’s own final visits shows the same ordering.

Reading of the diagnostic.

  • Thin final bins. The last 0–2 years before death hold at most 4 donors per tertile and are not drawn. The 2–4-year bin holds 11–22.
  • Different donors in different bins. Only 3 donors contribute to every bin from 0 to 8 years, so a fixed-donor version of the curves cannot be drawn.
  • The ordering is within-donor, not just composition. Over each donor’s own final ~4 years, memory declines faster in the higher tertiles (-0.048, -0.124 and -0.259 per year, low to high). The separation of the grouped curves reflects within-donor decline, not only who was seen when.
  • The late steepening is not an individual transition. The apparent late steepening of the high-tertile curve mixes donors with different visit timing, and high-tertile donors’ last visits fall earlier. It is not read as an individual-level acceleration or change point.

MEC is heavily involved early in almost every donor (Section 2), so its variation between donors is compressed. Memory decline reads as a stage-wide phenotype.

  • Visuospatial is unrelated to either (AnG, n = 34), which is unsurprising given its ceiling and poorly defined slope.

None of these comparisons shows that a region’s pathological distribution measures circuit function. They show which progression representation carries the domain’s association.

This section asks whether donors at the same CPS_Global_pTau but with different cognition differ in regional involvement or tissue response. The design is continuous and at donor level, with no resilience threshold and no matched cutoffs.

Reading. At comparable global pTau progression:

  • DFC involvement and terminal CASI: not robust to curvature. Donors with more DFC involvement have lower terminal CASI in the linear model (-0.40 [-0.70, -0.09] SD per SD). Once global pTau enters quadratically it attenuates to -0.25 [-0.60, +0.10]. DFC involvement rises mainly at high stage, where CASI falls fastest (Section 4.3), so this association is partly curvature in global progression, not regional involvement.
  • The executive pattern is regional and consistent in direction, but imprecise. Its primary intervals just reach zero and clear it only once curvature is allowed. More DFC involvement goes with faster executive decline (-0.34 [-0.71, +0.04]; with the quadratic -0.45 [-0.89, -0.01]). Relatively MEC-predominant tau goes with slower executive decline (+0.35 [-0.02, +0.72]; with the quadratic +0.54 [+0.08, +1.01]). MEC involvement beyond global stage is unrelated to terminal CASI (+0.14 [-0.18, +0.46]).
  • Consistency across representations. This matches the first-pass MEC-vs-neocortex AT8 gradient and the executive–DFC association of Section 4.4, on released rather than direct measures.
  • Direct donor-wide AT8 (-0.43 [-0.98, +0.12]) adds less beyond global pTau than it did beyond the Gabitto MTG CPS (Section 6). The released global pTau stage already captures most of the multiregional tau the first pass found missing from the MTG CPS.
  • Donor-wide NeuN: associated, but not separable from the severely affected phenotype.
    • Primary: higher donor-wide NeuN goes with better terminal CASI (+0.21 [+0.01, +0.40]) and slower memory decline (+0.23 [+0.02, +0.43]). It is nearly independent of global pTau (ρ -0.15).
    • Without the two NeuN-floor donors: memory rate is unchanged (+0.25 [+0.03, +0.46]).
    • Without all 8 severely affected ACT donors: +0.16 [-0.07, +0.38] and +0.19 [-0.06, +0.44], both intervals including zero.
    • With curvature in global pTau: +0.19 [-0.01, +0.40].
    The release describes these donors as having reduced NeuN labelling and steeper late memory decline (Section 3.4). This association therefore cannot be distinguished from that phenotype, and it is not carried forward as an independent tissue-integrity correlate of resilience.
  • Molecular response adds nothing clear. Donor-wide MG4 (-0.16 [-0.39, +0.08]) and astrocyte activation show no clear association beyond global stage.
  • Co-pathology leaves the pattern intact.
  • Collinearity is substantial (ρ with global pTau up to 0.94), so these are estimates of regional pattern at a given stage, with wide intervals.

First-pass conclusions, still standing:

  • Terminal vs longitudinal phenotypes. Pathology-adjusted memory decline largely reproduces notebook 04’s terminal residual, while executive decline is a partly separate axis.
  • Multiregional tau. At fixed MTG CPS, donor-wide direct AT8 is associated with worse terminal CASI, and MG4’s cognitive association weakens once that multiregional tau is included.
  • Matched pairs. Matching on the three-region AT8 profile narrowed matched CASI differences, and the MG4/NeuN differences in CPS-matched pairs reversed under profile matching. Pairs were illustrative only.

Section 5 shows that the released global pTau stage absorbs much of the multiregional tau that the MTG CPS missed.

7. Synthesis

1. What global and regional progression explain about cognition.

  • Global pTau stage carries most of the pathology–cognition association:
    • terminal CASI -0.24 [-0.31, -0.16] SD per 0.1;
    • global slope -0.21 [-0.29, -0.13];
    • memory rate -0.20 [-0.28, -0.12];
    • language rate -0.15 [-0.23, -0.07].
    These are robust to co-pathology. Terminal CASI and memory rate are concave in global stage (flat with a CASI ceiling early, steeper late). The linear estimate is an average association.
  • Conventional staging is too coarse to stand in for progression. Braak V and High ADNC each span most of the global range (32 of 34 Braak V donors overlap the Braak IV or VI range).
  • Matched regions add nothing for memory or language beyond global stage (memory: global -0.53 [-0.69, -0.35]).

2. What remains associated with cognition at comparable progression.

  • Executive decline, the one regionally structured phenotype:
    • faster with DFC involvement (-0.45 [-0.89, -0.01] with curvature allowed);
    • slower with MEC-predominant tau (+0.54 [+0.08, +1.01]).
    The direction holds across representations (direct AT8 in the first pass, released local pTau here) and under co-pathology and curvature. The primary linear intervals just reach zero, so the estimate is imprecise.
  • DFC–terminal CASI does not survive curvature in global stage (-0.25 [-0.60, +0.10]).
  • Donor-wide NeuN is associated with slower memory decline, but it cannot be separated from the published severely affected phenotype (Section 5).
  • Donor-wide MG4 and astrocyte activation add nothing clear.

3. What MG4 and NeuN currently support biologically.

  • MG4 is a donor-level microglial state that scales with global pTau stage (+0.36 [+0.20, +0.51] SD/SD). It is not a regional one (within-donor +0.16 [-0.08, +0.37]), and it carries no cognitive information beyond stage. It is a marker of disease stage, not an established protective or harmful factor.
  • NeuN immunoreactive density is modestly lower where local pTau is higher within donors (-0.13 [-0.33, +0.08], interval reaching zero). MG4 at comparable local pathology is at most weakly positive for it (+0.09 [-0.06, +0.23]).
  • The two donors with near-zero NeuN show a severe neuronal phenotype: reduced NeuN immunoreactivity, and low neuronal representation in snRNA-seq from donors defined partly by poor nuclei QC. Absolute neuronal loss is neither established nor excluded. NeuN density measures NeuN-immunoreactive profiles, not neuron number or synaptic integrity.

4. Which aspects of the cognitive measurements remain uncertain.

  • Domain scores. Documented as co-calibrated CFA/IRT scores with per-score SEs. Their reference mean/SD and the calibration release used here are not documented.
  • Slopes. No accessible source documents the model, time scale, units or uncertainty of any released slope, so associations are reported in SD of the released variable.
  • Visuospatial. Dominated by a single scored pattern (58% of visits), empirically consistent with a ceiling on a small item set. The item content and battery history are undocumented.
  • Visit timing. Whole-year ages, a thin final two years before death, and grouped curves that pool different donors limit any claim about terminal acceleration.
